container_length: float (JSON number; integer or decimal allowed); container length L, finite and strictly greater than 0; unit is the instance-wide length unit U_l, whose physical unit is unspecified; scalar, no array index, corresponds to the spatial x-axis. All box edge lengths and the x, y, z coordinates in the solution use the same U_l.
container_width: float (JSON number; integer or decimal allowed); container width W, finite and strictly greater than 0; unit is U_l, the same as container_length; scalar, no array index, corresponds to the spatial y-axis.
container_height: float (JSON number; integer or decimal allowed); container height H, finite and strictly greater than 0; unit is U_l, the same as container_length; scalar, no array index, corresponds to the vertically upward spatial z-axis.
num_box_types: int (JSON integer; booleans not accepted); number of box types N, N >= 0, 0 allowed; unit: types; scalar, does not correspond to a spatial axis. Box type index i ranges from 0 to N-1; every input array indexed by box type must have outer length exactly N, and when N=0 all these arrays are [].
box_quantities: list[int]; length exactly N, the only array axis is box type i; item i is the upper limit q_i on the number of candidate boxes of that type, a non-negative integer, booleans not accepted, unit: boxes. A single item or all items may be 0. Candidate box index k of that type ranges from 0 to q_i-1; when q_i=0 there are no candidate boxes of that type. The quantity is an upper limit on how many may be loaded, not a demand that must be loaded.
box_lengths: list[float] (elements are JSON numbers; integer or decimal allowed); length exactly N, the only array axis is box type i; item i is the original length of boxes of that type, finite and strictly greater than 0, unit U_l. This field denotes an original edge and is not tied to a fixed spatial axis after placement: it becomes dz under orientation 1 and dx under orientations 2 and 3; it is not required to be the largest of the three original edges.
box_widths: list[float] (elements are JSON numbers; integer or decimal allowed); length exactly N, the only array axis is box type i; item i is the original width of boxes of that type, finite and strictly greater than 0, unit U_l. It becomes dx under orientation 1, dz under orientation 2, and dy under orientation 3.
box_heights: list[float] (elements are JSON numbers; integer or decimal allowed); length exactly N, the only array axis is box type i; item i is the original height of boxes of that type, finite and strictly greater than 0, unit U_l. It becomes dy under orientations 1 and 2, and dz under orientation 3.
box_weights: list[float] (elements are JSON numbers; integer or decimal allowed); length exactly N, the only array axis is box type i; item i is the self-weight of each box of that type, finite and strictly greater than 0, zero weight not allowed; unit is the instance-wide weight unit U_w, whose physical unit is unspecified. Every candidate box of the same type has the same self-weight.
orientation_allowed: list[list[int]]; shape exactly N×3; the first array axis is box type i, and second-axis indices r=0, 1, 2 correspond to orientation numbers o=1, 2, 3 respectively. Elements may only be the integers 0 or 1, booleans not accepted, dimensionless; 1 means allowed, 0 means forbidden; a row of all 0s is allowed. Orientation 1 has the original length vertical, with occupied dimensions (dx,dy,dz)=(box_widths[i],box_heights[i],box_lengths[i]); orientation 2 has the original width vertical, with occupied dimensions (box_lengths[i],box_heights[i],box_widths[i]); orientation 3 has the original height vertical, with occupied dimensions (box_lengths[i],box_widths[i],box_heights[i]). dx, dy, dz lie along the spatial x, y, z axes respectively; additionally swapping the two horizontal edges or any other rotation is not allowed.
load_bearing_by_orientation: list[list[float]] (elements are JSON numbers; integer or decimal allowed); shape exactly N×3; the first array axis is box type i, and second-axis indices r=0, 1, 2 correspond to orientation numbers o=1, 2, 3 respectively. All elements must be finite non-negative reals, 0 allowed; even if the corresponding orientation is forbidden, the component must still be present and meet the same value requirement. Each element is an upper limit on load per unit area, not on total weight; unit is U_w/U_l², which must be consistent with the length and weight units used by all inputs and coordinates, and the value is used directly in computation. A box's actual total load-bearing limit is its top-face area dx×dy in the current orientation multiplied by component o-1 of this field; the load borne is the cumulative self-weight of all boxes above it transmitted along the support relations, excluding the box's own weight.
